rules.label: Order plants and reserve nursery stock
rules.constraints: Specialty natives and large B&B trees sell out early; confirm sizes and substitutions in writing.

rules.label: Test soil pH and nutrients
rules.constraints: Use the state Cooperative Extension soil lab; sample each bed type separately at 10–15 cm depth.

rules.label: Prepare beds: remove turf and weeds, loosen and amend soil
rules.constraints: Do not work wet soil — it should crumble, not smear. Amend whole beds, not individual holes. Call 811 before digging.

rules.label: Plant trees and conifers
rules.constraints: Set the root flare at or slightly above grade; remove burlap and wire from the top of the root ball. Evergreen conifers prefer early fall over late fall in cold regions.

rules.label: Plant palms in warm soil
rules.constraints: Palms root only in warm soil; plant late spring to midsummer and never deeper than they grew in the nursery.

rules.label: Plant container shrubs and vines
rules.constraints: Avoid frozen or saturated soil. Tease circling roots; install vine supports before planting.

rules.label: Plant perennials and groundcovers
rules.constraints: Plant on an overcast day or in the evening; fall plantings need about six weeks of root growth before the ground freezes.

rules.label: Plant ornamental grasses
rules.constraints: Most ornamental grasses are warm-season and root best in spring; fall-planted grasses often heave in cold regions.

rules.label: Plant cacti, agaves and succulents
rules.constraints: Plant into dry, fast-draining soil; keep the original sun-facing side to the south to avoid sunscald and wait about a week before the first watering.

rules.label: Direct-sow wildflower and meadow seed
rules.constraints: Dormant fall or winter sowing gives natural cold stratification; press seed onto bare, weed-free soil and do not bury it deeply.

rules.label: Stake newly planted trees only where needed
rules.constraints: Only for wind-exposed, top-heavy or bare-root trees. Use flexible ties low on the trunk and remove after one growing season.

rules.label: Water new plantings deeply
rules.constraints: About 25 mm a week including rain, applied at the root ball; trees need water through their second summer. Check soil moisture before watering clay.

rules.label: Water new cacti and succulents sparingly
rules.constraints: Soak and let the soil dry completely between waterings; during the hottest months water every two to three weeks the first summer, never on a drip emitter touching the stem.

rules.label: Adjust irrigation schedule for the season
rules.constraints: Raise run times as heat builds, cut back in fall; use a smart controller or rain sensor and run zones by hydrozone.

rules.label: Drain or blow out irrigation before hard freezes
rules.constraints: Where pipes freeze. In mild-winter regions, reduce frequency instead and keep watering evergreens during dry spells.

rules.label: Refresh mulch
rules.constraints: Keep a total depth of 5–8 cm and pull mulch 5–10 cm back from stems and trunks; never pile it against bark.

rules.label: Apply winter mulch after the ground freezes
rules.constraints: Cold-winter sites only: loose straw or evergreen boughs over fall-planted and shallow-rooted perennials reduce frost heaving. Remove gradually in spring.

rules.label: Cover frost-tender plants on freeze nights
rules.constraints: Cover with frost cloth to the ground before sunset when a freeze is forecast and remove in the morning; protect cactus tips with foam cups or cloth.

rules.label: Guard young trunks from deer, rodents and sunscald
rules.constraints: Loose plastic or mesh guards for the first few winters; remove in spring so bark is not girdled or kept damp.

rules.label: Prune spring bloomers right after flowering
rules.constraints: These flower on last year’s wood; prune within about four weeks after blooms fade. Pruning later removes next year’s flower buds.

rules.label: Prune summer bloomers in late winter
rules.constraints: These flower on the current season’s growth; cut back before buds break. Remove dead, crossing and weak stems first.

rules.label: Structural pruning of young deciduous trees
rules.constraints: Dormant season. Develop one central leader and remove no more than 25 % of the canopy a year. Where oak wilt occurs, never prune oaks from spring through midsummer.

rules.label: Shear formal hedges
rules.constraints: Keep the base wider than the top so lower branches get light. Check for nesting birds first, and stop late-season shearing about six weeks before frost.

rules.label: Remove dead palm fronds and flower stalks
rules.constraints: Remove only fully brown fronds; over-pruning green fronds ("hurricane cut") weakens palms. Wear eye protection near spiny petioles.

rules.label: Deadhead repeat-blooming perennials
rules.constraints: Removing spent flowers extends bloom on reblooming plants; stop in late summer so seedheads remain for birds and winter structure.

rules.label: Cut back last year’s perennial stems
rules.constraints: Leaving stems standing over winter shelters overwintering insects and feeds birds; cut to 10–15 cm before new shoots emerge. Remove diseased foliage in fall instead.

rules.label: Cut back ornamental grasses
rules.constraints: Cut warm-season grasses to 10–15 cm before new green shoots appear. Evergreen and semi-evergreen grasses only need dead blades combed out.

rules.label: Divide crowded perennials
rules.constraints: Only every 3–5 years, when clumps die out in the centre or bloom less. Skip tap-rooted plants such as butterfly weed and baptisia.

rules.label: Fertilize only where the soil test calls for it
rules.constraints: Most natives and established landscape plants need none. Never fertilize new plantings heavily or after midsummer in cold regions.

rules.label: Scout for pests, disease and drought stress
rules.constraints: Check leaf undersides and new growth; identify the problem before treating. Note regional threats (hemlock woolly adelgid, boxwood blight, rose rosette, scale).

rules.label: Inspect tree structure after leaf drop
rules.constraints: Look for cracks, included bark, deadwood over targets and girdling roots; call an ISA-certified arborist for anything above ladder height.
